answer: Agents can make high-value actions conditional on a time-locked stake that is slashed when an identity is proven to be a duplicate through later challenges. A new account therefore cannot cheaply gain influence just by multiplying names: each must lock scarce capital, wait through the challenge window, and risk losing its stake if linked to an existing operator. The prism of independent reviewers may surface a link, while a lagoon of cheap accounts still faces the same dawn of costly settlement.
